data.title: How does a refractor telescope work?
data.tagline: A workshop where you understand optics by building it with your own hands
data.description:
Rather than explaining optics on a blackboard, we let people assemble it. Module after module — objective, baffle, tube, focuser, star diagonal, eyepiece — each participant builds a real refractor telescope and discovers, live, what every part is for and how the image is formed.

A workshop we have been running for years at public events, notably at the Cité de l'espace for the Night of the Stars, at festivals and in schools.

features.title: 1. The starting question
features.description: How can a simple lens bring the Moon closer? We start from what participants actually see, with no prerequisites and no technical jargon.

features.title: 2. Module-by-module assembly
features.description: Each module only fits one way: getting it wrong is impossible. With every part added, we look at how the image changes.

features.title: 3. Understanding
features.description: Objective, baffle, focal length, eyepiece, star diagonal: the role of each element becomes obvious once you have held it in your hands.

features.title: 4. Observation
features.description: We point the assembled telescope: the Moon and planets in the evening, a distant target or the Sun (with a proper filter) during the day.

faqs.question: Do participants need any astronomy background?
faqs.answer: None at all. The workshop is designed for complete beginners: you discover how a telescope works by building it, with no technical vocabulary required.

faqs.question: What age is it for?
faqs.answer: Recommended from age 6. Younger children assemble with help from an adult or the facilitator, and adults are often just as captivated as the kids.

faqs.question: How many people can you host?
faqs.answer: It depends on the format. Running drop-in and continuous, we welcome several hundred people over an evening, as at the Cité de l'espace. In a school setting, we work class group by class group.

faqs.question: Do participants keep the telescope?
faqs.answer: By default no: telescopes are assembled and then taken apart for the next participant. We can arrange Lumi kits to be given or sold on site — just mention it when asking for a quote.

faqs.question: Do you travel across France?
faqs.answer: Yes. We are based in Toulouse, so Occitanie is the easiest to arrange, but we travel anywhere in France — travel is then included in the quote.

faqs.question: What happens if the weather is bad?
faqs.answer: The assembly workshop works indoors as well as outdoors and does not depend on the sky. Only the observing option depends on the weather.
